Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Fernhollow Photo is a real business now!!

Okay, deep breath. I have news, and I wanted to write it here instead of announcing it over the turkey at Ruthie’s while everybody is holding a serving spoon.

I’m going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo is a real business now!!

Like, actually real. I filed Fernhollow Photo LLC on October 22, and the website went live on November 1. It feels very strange and exciting to type that instead of just thinking about it, which is what I’ve been doing for approximately forever.

The actual filing was extremely glamorous, by the way. I did it on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer. Then I cried a little. Not because anything went wrong—just because there was suddenly a name and an LLC and a real thing where there used to be an idea I carried around in my head. Then I went back to work, because apparently even business owners have to finish their lunch breaks.

Sam made me a cake to celebrate. It was supposed to say FERNHOLLOW, but one of the Ls went missing somewhere in the decorating process, so it said FERNHOLOW. We ate it anyway, obviously. So my official business origin story now involves a parked car, a Fred Meyer, some crying, and a missing L. Honestly, that feels about right.

For anyone wondering about the name: Fernhollow comes from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma’s old place in Gresham. That’s where I took my first real pictures with her Pentax. Before weddings, before all the cameras and lenses and memory cards, before this was even something I knew a person could do for a living, there was that trail and that camera.

Grandma, the name is for you. I hope you like it. Every time I say it or type it or put it on something, that’s where it comes from.

Some of you know that I’ve spent the last four years shooting weddings for Marisol at Rosebud Lane. Marisol told me on October 6 that she would be closing the studio at the end of October. I won’t pretend that news didn’t knock the wind out of me. Rosebud Lane has been a huge part of my life, and four years is a lot of wedding days, late nights, sore knees, and learning on the fly.

Marisol basically taught me everything I know about this work. Not just how to use a camera or find good light, but how to keep a wedding day moving, how to stay calm when things aren’t going according to plan, and how to take care of people while also doing the job. She trusted me with her couples and gave me room to get better. I’m incredibly grateful for that, and anything good I build with Fernhollow is going to have some of what I learned at Rosebud Lane in it.

She has also been unbelievably generous with her trust during this change. Six of the weddings I have booked for next year came through referrals from Marisol. That means a lot to me. Those aren’t just names on a calendar; they’re couples she believed I could take care of, and I don’t take that lightly.

Now, the practical part, because I want you all to be excited with me and not quietly worrying at home.

Dad, before you start preparing the health insurance speech: health insurance is sorted. I picked a marketplace plan on November 5, and my coverage starts January 1. You can still ask me about it if you want, but you don’t have to save the whole speech for Thanksgiving dinner. Maybe we can just eat pie instead.

I know owning a business can sound like I’ve decided to run full speed off a cliff with a camera bag, but this isn’t a sudden decision. I’ve been planning it in my head for two years. It is scary. I’m not going to pretend it isn’t. But scary and reckless aren’t the same thing, and I have a plan.

As of right now, I have 14 weddings booked for 2027. Six are Marisol referrals, and eight found me on my own. That second number makes me want to happy-cry all over again. The deposits so far total $9,800. June is currently my busiest month, with four weddings, and the farthest booking on the calendar is at Wallowa Lake in September. For the bigger weddings, Jae will second shoot with me, paid per wedding, so I’m not planning to handle absolutely everything alone.

The first booking that was 100% mine was Dahlia + Ken. They’re getting married at Timberline on June 12, and they found me through the Multnomah Falls couple pictures I took while working with Marisol. That booking meant so much to me—not because a referral is somehow less meaningful, but because they saw the work and chose me before Fernhollow was even a name on a website. It made this whole thing feel possible in a different way.

So yes, I’m nervous. I’m also really, really excited. I get to keep doing the work I love, under a name that means something to me, and I already have real couples trusting me with real days. That’s the part I keep coming back to whenever my brain starts spinning.

One more thing: I’m bringing my camera to Thanksgiving at Ruthie’s, and if anybody wants family pictures, they’re on me. Totally free. We can do the whole crew, smaller family groups, grandparents with grandkids, you and your person, your kids, whatever you want. You don’t have to dress up or buy anything or pretend you enjoy having your picture taken. Just find me and I’ll find some decent light. I’ll do the big group photo too if everybody wants one. Uncle Greg, I’ll try to be efficient.

I wanted everyone to hear this from me first, with the actual details, so it doesn’t turn into a game of telephone before we even get to Salem. Please ask me questions. Please be excited with me. Dad, please also remember the part about January 1.

Love you all. See you at Thanksgiving—and if Fernhollow ever gets a real sign, I’m checking the spelling twice.
